subsectors.name: Performing Arts, Spectator Sports, and Related Industries

codes.organization: SAG-AFTRA (Screen Actors Guild - American Federation of Television and Radio Artists)
codes.notes: Union code governing member conduct. Updated post-#MeToo. Covers workplace harassment, professional behavior, and solidarity obligations. Also issued separate Code of Ethics for Talent Managers.

codes.document_title: Standards and Protocols for the Use of Intimacy Coordinators
codes.notes: February 2024 update formalizing consent, safety, and professionalism protocols for scenes involving nudity or simulated intimacy.

codes.document_title: Codes, Guidelines and Internal Membership Rules
codes.notes: Union for professional actors and stage managers in live theater. Covers member obligations re punctuality, professional conduct, dispute resolution via Deputies and Business Representatives.
Covers 7,800+ managers of arenas, stadiums, performing arts centers, convention centers, and amphitheaters. Required affirmation for CVE/CVP certification.
Article 10 of NCAA Constitution covers ethical conduct in college athletics: honesty, sportsmanship, anti-gambling, reporting violations.

codes.organization: North American Society for Sport Management (NASSM)
codes.notes: Academic and professional body for sport management. Covers research integrity, professional competence, and social responsibility in sport.
Governs athletes, coaches, officials, and staff. Strong SafeSport provisions on abuse, harassment, and athlete welfare.

subsectors.name: Museums, Historical Sites, and Similar Institutions

codes.notes: Adopted 1993, revised 2000. Fundamental to AAM accreditation. Covers governance, collections stewardship, public trust, and institutional integrity. All museums regardless of size expected to follow.

codes.document_title: ICOM Code of Ethics for Museums
codes.notes: Global standard adopted 1986, revised 2004. 8 principles covering institutional governance, acquisition, due diligence for provenance, cultural property protection, community engagement. Translated into 38 languages.
Required for AZA accreditation. Covers animal welfare, conservation mission, honest communication, and ethical treatment of wildlife. AZA accredits 240+ facilities.

codes.document_title: SAA Core Values Statement and Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Covers archival professionals at museums, historical sites, and cultural institutions. Emphasizes access, accountability, diversity, preservation, and responsible custody.

codes.organization: Association of Registrars and Collections Specialists (ARCS)
codes.notes: Ethics for museum registrars and collections managers handling acquisitions, loans, and de-accessions. Covers fiduciary duty, provenance research, and conflict of interest.

Updated regularly (2026 version published Dec 2025). Member companies pledge responsible gaming in daily operations. Covers underage gambling prevention, self-exclusion, employee training, and advertising ethics.

codes.document_title: Responsible Marketing Code for Sports Wagering
codes.notes: Specific code for sports betting advertising and marketing. Covers truthfulness, targeting restrictions, and responsible messaging.

codes.organization: International Association of Amusement Parks and Attractions (IAAPA)
codes.notes: Global attractions industry. Covers quality products/services, fact-based communications, truthful advertising, conflict of interest avoidance, social and environmental responsibility.
Code of conduct for Certified Park and Recreation Professionals (CPRP). Covers ethical standards for parks, recreation, and leisure services professionals.

codes.document_title: NIGC Regulations — Minimum Internal Control Standards
codes.notes: Federal regulatory standards for tribal gaming operations. Includes ethical conduct provisions for gaming employees, anti-fraud measures, and integrity of gaming operations.

codes.document_title: AHLA Safe Stay Guidelines and Ethics Standards
codes.notes: Industry guidelines covering employee conduct, anti-trafficking measures, and guest safety. AHLA also maintains the 5-Star Promise on employee safety and anti-harassment. Specific ethics code not publicly posted as standalone document.

codes.organization: International Hotel & Restaurant Association (IH&RA) / International Hospitality Institute
codes.document_title: Code of Ethics for the Hospitality Industry
codes.notes: Global hospitality ethics framework. Covers guest safety, employee welfare, environmental sustainability, and fair business practices. IH&RA represents hotels in 150+ countries.
Covers financial and technology professionals in hospitality. Addresses integrity, competence, confidentiality, and professional objectivity for hotel finance/IT staff.

codes.document_title: ServSafe Food Handler Ethical Standards and Event Code of Conduct
codes.notes: The NRA does not publish a standalone industry-wide code of ethics but maintains ServSafe certification standards for food safety and an event code of conduct. Historical 1930s 'Code of Fair Competition' established early ethical expectations.
Covers manufacturers, importers, distributors, and retailers of specialty foods. Mandates honest advertising, fair dealing, respect for competitors and customers.
Ethics code for restaurant facility management professionals. Covers professional integrity, competence, and responsible facility stewardship.
Covers Certified Dietary Managers and foodservice professionals in institutional settings (hospitals, schools, care facilities). Focuses on food safety, nutrition integrity, and client welfare.

codes.organization: National Institute for Automotive Service Excellence (ASE)
codes.notes: All ASE-certified technicians pledge to uphold this code. Covers first-class workmanship, lifelong learning, customer welfare, recommending only necessary work, and maintaining public respect for the profession. Embedded in ASE certification process.
HVAC contractors. Covers honest representation, fair pricing, quality workmanship, environmental responsibility, and continuing education.
Covers electronics technicians and certified professionals in repair and maintenance of electronic equipment. Emphasizes honesty, competence, and fair dealing.
While primarily construction, covers remodeling and home repair/maintenance. Covers quality workmanship, fair dealing, compliance with building codes, and customer satisfaction.

Professional code for licensed barbers. Covers sanitation, client confidentiality, professional competence, and community responsibility. Part of the American Barber Certification Council (ABCC) program.

Binding on NFDA members. Covers obligations to family, care of decedent, public, government, and NFDA. Violations subject to disciplinary action. Addresses pricing transparency and pre-need arrangements.

codes.organization: National Association of Productivity and Organizing Professionals (NAPO)
codes.notes: Professional organizers and productivity consultants. Covers client confidentiality, competence, integrity, reasonable fees, and professional boundaries.

codes.organization: International Cemetery, Cremation and Funeral Association (ICCFA)
codes.notes: Covers cemetery, cremation, and funeral service professionals internationally. Emphasizes dignity, transparency in pricing, and respect for diverse cultural and religious practices.

codes.organization: National Association of Professional Pet Sitters (NAPPS)
codes.notes: All NAPPS members must adhere to a code of ethics covering animal welfare, client confidentiality, professionalism, and responsible pet care.

subsectors.name: Religious, Grantmaking, Civic, Professional, and Similar Organizations

codes.notes: Board approved December 2023, now enforceable. All AFP members required to sign. Covers donor rights, stewardship, solicitation ethics, and fiduciary responsibility. 26 specific standards.

codes.document_title: Statement of Values and Code of Ethics for Nonprofit and Philanthropic Organizations
codes.notes: Foundational ethics framework for the nonprofit sector. Covers public good commitment, accountability beyond the law, responsible stewardship, openness, inclusiveness, and fundraising ethics.

codes.organization: Standards for Excellence Institute / Independent Sector
codes.document_title: Standards for Excellence: An Ethics and Accountability Code for the Nonprofit Sector
codes.notes: Comprehensive ethics and accountability code. 6 categories: Mission/Strategy, Leadership, Ethics/Legal, Finance/Operations, Resource Development, Public Awareness. Online self-assessment available.

codes.document_title: Ethics and Accountability for Nonprofits — Principles and Standards
codes.notes: Compiles ethical standards from state associations of nonprofits. Covers governance, financial transparency, donor stewardship, and organizational accountability.

codes.document_title: ASAE Standards of Conduct — Core Ethical Standards
codes.notes: Governs conduct for leaders of professional and trade associations. Covers basic conduct, confidentiality, competition, giving/receiving, and member relations. Updated September 2022.

codes.document_title: Principles and Practices for Effective Grantmaking
codes.notes: Ethical framework for foundations and grantmaking organizations. Covers donor intent, effective governance, transparency, responsible investment, and legal compliance.

7 standards for evangelical Christian nonprofit organizations. Covers doctrinal commitment, governance, financial oversight, truthful communication, and responsible stewardship. 2,600+ accredited members.

codes.document_title: Nonprofit Board Member Codes of Conduct and Ethics
codes.notes: Model code for nonprofit board governance. Covers fiduciary duty, conflict of interest, confidentiality, duty of care, and board member accountability.

codes.document_title: INA Recommended Practices — Code of Ethical Conduct
codes.notes: Covers professional nannies. Addresses child welfare, confidentiality, professional development, family/employer relationships, and ethical boundaries. INA Credentialed Nanny designation.

codes.document_title: Domestic Workers Bill of Rights — Ethical Standards Framework
codes.notes: Framework for fair and ethical treatment of household workers (nannies, house cleaners, caregivers). Covers fair wages, safe working conditions, freedom from harassment, and privacy. Adopted as law in 10+ states.

subsectors.name: Executive, Legislative, and Other General Government Support

codes.document_title: Standards of Ethical Conduct for Employees of the Executive Branch
codes.notes: 5 CFR Part 2635. Binding federal regulation. Based on Executive Order 12731 (1990). Modernization updates published May 2024. Covers gifts, conflicts of interest, outside employment, misuse of position. Applies to all 2M+ executive branch employees.

8 principles: advance public interest, uphold Constitution, promote democratic participation, strengthen social equity, fully inform, demonstrate personal integrity, promote ethical organizations, advance professional excellence. Ethics Implementation Committee since 2014.

codes.document_title: ICMA Code of Ethics with Guidelines
codes.notes: Adopted 1924 — among the oldest professional ethics codes in public administration. 12 tenets covering democratic government, public trust, political neutrality, equity, transparency, and professional development. ICMA enforces through ethics investigations.
Model code for county officials. Covers public trust, impartiality, transparency, proper use of public resources, and avoiding conflicts of interest.

codes.organization: United Nations — International Civil Service Commission (ICSC)
codes.document_title: Standards of Conduct for the International Civil Service
codes.notes: Applies to all UN system employees. Replaces 1954/2001 editions. Covers independence, impartiality, integrity, accountability, respect for diversity, non-discrimination, and conflicts of interest. Translated into 6 official UN languages.
Covers government finance officers in the US and Canada. Addresses honest financial management, transparency, prudent use of public funds, avoiding conflicts of interest, and professional competence.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics for City Officials
codes.notes: Model ethics code for municipal elected and appointed officials. Covers public trust, transparency, conflict of interest, impartiality, and proper use of public office.

subsectors.name: Justice, Public Order, and Safety Activities

codes.organization: International Association of Chiefs of Police (IACP)
codes.notes: Originally adopted 1957 at 64th IACP Conference, updated 2024. Foundational document for law enforcement worldwide. Covers primary duty to serve, confidentiality, use of force, impartiality, and personal conduct. Widely adopted by US police departments.

codes.organization: International Association of Chiefs of Police (IACP)
codes.notes: Short-form ethical pledge for law enforcement. Emphasizes integrity, bravery, honor, and treating all persons with dignity and respect. Part of IACP Ethics Toolkit.

codes.document_title: Fire Service Professional Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Covers fire service leadership. Establishes criteria encouraging personnel to promote a culture of ethical integrity and high standards of professionalism. Separate Firefighter Code of Ethics also maintained.

codes.organization: National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) / National Fallen Firefighters Foundation
codes.notes: Joint initiative. Covers all fire service personnel. Addresses integrity, accountability, leadership, professional competence, community service, and personal conduct on and off duty.

Covers corrections professionals. Requires honesty, respect for dignity of individuals, commitment to professional service, protection of civil/legal rights, and reporting corrupt or unethical behavior.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics for Jail Officers
codes.notes: Specific to jail officers. Covers duty as good citizens, professional conduct, respect for incarcerated persons' rights, and commitment to community.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics for the Field of Community Corrections
codes.notes: Covers probation, parole, and community corrections officers. Addresses public safety, offender rehabilitation, professional integrity, and fair administration of justice.

codes.document_title: IAEM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
codes.notes: Covers emergency management professionals (CEM/AEM certified). Addresses public safety, professional competence, ethical decision-making in crisis, and cooperation across agencies.

4th edition. Chapter 1 covers ethical obligations of prosecutors: duty to seek justice not merely convict, disclosure obligations, avoiding conflicts, and professional conduct. Supplements ABA Model Rules.

codes.organization: National Association of State Workforce Agencies (NASWA)
codes.document_title: NASWA Code of Ethics and Professional Standards
codes.notes: Covers state-level administrators of unemployment insurance, employment services, and workforce development programs. Emphasis on equitable service delivery, data privacy, and program integrity.

While primarily covering professional social workers (NAICS 62), directly relevant to public administration of human services programs. Covers service, social justice, dignity, human relationships, integrity, and competence. 155 standards in 6 sections.

codes.organization: International Public Management Association for Human Resources (IPMA-HR)
codes.notes: Covers public sector HR professionals administering civil service, benefits, and employment programs. Addresses merit-based systems, non-discrimination, confidentiality, and professional development.

codes.document_title: NEHA Member Code of Ethics / Credential Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Covers environmental health professionals (sanitarians, health inspectors). Separate credential code for REHS/RS holders. Covers continuing education, public health protection, and professional integrity.

codes.document_title: NAEP Code of Ethics and Standards of Practice
codes.notes: Covers environmental impact assessment professionals, NEPA practitioners, and environmental compliance officers in government. Covers scientific integrity, transparency, and public interest.

codes.organization: Institute of Environmental Management and Assessment (IEMA)
codes.notes: International body for environmental and sustainability professionals. Covers professional competence, ethical decision-making, environmental stewardship, and public interest. 15,000+ members in 100+ countries.

subsectors.name: Administration of Housing Programs, Urban Planning, and Community Development

codes.organization: American Institute of Certified Planners (AICP) / American Planning Association (APA)
codes.document_title: AICP Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
codes.notes: Adopted 2005, revised 2021. Three-part structure: aspirational principles (all planners), rules of conduct (AICP members), and enforcement procedures. Covers social justice, expanding choice and opportunity, racial and economic integration.

codes.organization: National Association of Housing and Redevelopment Officials (NAHRO)
codes.document_title: NAHRO Code of Professional Conduct and Ethics
codes.notes: Covers professionals in public housing, community development, and housing redevelopment agencies. Addresses fair housing, tenant welfare, transparency, and proper use of public funds.
Covers building code enforcement officers in housing and urban development. Addresses impartial enforcement, due process, professional competence, and public safety.
Covers economic development professionals. Addresses integrity, honesty, public trust, professional competence, and responsible development. Enforcement procedures in place.
Also listed under 925. Primary code for economic development professionals. Members pledge integrity, objectivity, and bringing respect to the profession.

All AAPC members required to sign annually. Sets standards for campaign and business practices to promote integrity and confidence in the political system. Relevant to government economic program administration.

codes.organization: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
codes.notes: Framework for government integrity in economic program administration. 13 principles covering commitment, responsibilities, strategic approach, standards, merit-based employment, and risk management. Adopted by 38 OECD member countries.

codes.document_title: NASA Ethics Program — Standards of Ethical Conduct
codes.notes: NASA employees subject to 5 CFR Part 2635 (government-wide) plus 5 CFR Part 6901 (NASA-specific supplemental standards). Covers outside employment approval, financial disclosure, contractor relations, and scientific integrity.

codes.document_title: NASA Supplemental Standards of Ethical Conduct
codes.notes: 5 CFR Part 6901. Agency-specific regulations supplementing OGE standards. Requires prior approval for outside employment and addresses NASA-specific conflicts of interest.

codes.document_title: Guidelines for Promoting Scientific and Research Integrity
codes.notes: Covers scientific misconduct, research data integrity, peer review ethics, and responsible authorship. Applies to all NASA-funded research.

Updated May 2024. Comprehensive ethics regulation for all DoD military and civilian personnel. Covers gifts, outside activities, financial interests, post-government employment, political activities, and standards of conduct.

codes.document_title: Code of Conduct for Members of the Armed Forces of the United States
codes.notes: Executive Order 10631 (1955), amended by EO 12633 (1988). 6 articles covering duty, surrender, captivity, and resistance. Applies to all US military personnel at all times. Foundational military ethics document.

codes.organization: United Nations — International Civil Service Commission (ICSC)
codes.document_title: Standards of Conduct for the International Civil Service
codes.notes: Also listed under 921. Applies to UN personnel in peacekeeping, international security, and diplomatic roles. Covers independence, impartiality, integrity, and conduct during international operations.

codes.document_title: CIA Values — Ethics and Integrity Standards
codes.notes: CIA's stated values include Service, Integrity, Excellence, Courage, Teamwork, and Stewardship. Subject to Intelligence Community Directive 120 on intelligence community ethics. Detailed internal ethics code not publicly released.

codes.document_title: Principles of Professional Ethics for the Intelligence Community
codes.notes: Issued by the Director of National Intelligence. Covers all 18 US intelligence agencies. Addresses mission integrity, truth, lawfulness, objectivity, accountability, and stewardship. Classified annexes supplement the public document.
